attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I feel positive about this paper. My overall impression is good, and I'd be pleased to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-dxlmlj79/call-a41af107ded640ccb62e19724da8e299/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && file manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'
/bin/bash -c "python3 -c \"import importlib.util; print({m:importlib.util.find_spec(m) is not None for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']})\""

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n'+(p.extract_text() or ''))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text[:3]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c "rg -n -i 'held.out|validation|test set|test.set|error bars|standard deviation|standard error|confidence|percentile|each dot|each point|200k|4k' tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for n in range(1,22):
    (p / f'page-{n:02d}.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p / 'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: The per-orientation heatmaps reveal informative structure that aggregate accuracy obscures: generalization concentrates around familiar views, in-plane rotations, and certain silhouette-preserving transformations. These findings have a clear audience in visual robustness and representation learning.

The experimental coverage is substantial: three object categories, three network architectures, different training orientation ranges, cross-category transfer, pretraining, augmentation, and reduced-data controls. Five repetitions and a fixed total training budget strengthen the descriptive evidence.

The geometric model provides an interpretable account of the observed patterns, with reported correlations above 0.8 across the main conditions. Component ablations help distinguish the contributions of small-angle, in-plane, and silhouette-related transformations.
The experimental paradigm and main visualizations communicate the behavioral findings effectively. The manuscript also supplies mathematical definitions and a public code/data link.
weaknesses: Necessary: The central mechanistic claims exceed the evidence. Figure 4 and Figure S.7 establish associations among activation similarity, orientation, and accuracy; they do not establish that particular shared-feature neurons causally disseminate invariance from fully-seen to partially-seen instances. Similar responses can also reflect common image geometry or joint learning. The abstract and discussion should frame dissemination as a supported hypothesis and biological parallels as an interpretation. Retaining stronger causal claims would require targeted interventions with appropriate controls.

Necessary: Predictive validation is insufficiently specified. Section 4.2 optimizes the geometric model's parameters using Pearson correlation with network accuracy, then reports that correlation as predictive evidence without describing an independent evaluation split. The reported values therefore establish goodness of fit, but do not establish prediction of unseen experimental outcomes. Specify the fitting/evaluation protocol and provide independent evaluation, or consistently present the model as a retrospective description. Defining generalizable orientations using this fitted model also means their subsequent accuracy contrast is not an independent validation.

Necessary: The invariance statistic needs stronger validation or narrower interpretation. Equations 5–8 compare activation means across orientation sets, so a neuron can receive a high score despite substantial variation within each set. Requiring both means to exceed the activity threshold also excludes neurons whose responses disappear outside the training orientations. Report the retained fractions and threshold sensitivity, and substantiate invariance at finer orientation resolution before interpreting these conditional mean similarities as preservation of the features responsible for recognition.

Necessary reporting improvements: Specify test-set sizes and generation, numerical orientation-bin resolution, what the error bars represent, and the experimental units and aggregation underlying Figure 4. The text describes points as instances or orientations, while Equation 7 averages over neurons and instances; this connection needs clarification to assess uncertainty and reproduce the analysis.

Optional improvements: A control holding the number of fully-seen training images fixed would help separate instance diversity from increased exposure to broadly distributed orientations: with 4,000 images per instance, increasing fully-seen instances from 10 to 40 increases that exposure fourfold despite constant total data. More naturalistic rendering and evaluation under uniform sampling on SO(3), rather than uniform Euler angles, would further characterize scope. These extensions are not prerequisites for publishing appropriately bounded findings.
